17592186069577}} {:db/id 17592186069960 :tutorial/content "A function $f(x)$ is said to be **right-continuous** at the point $x=c$ if the right-sided limit is equal to the function value:

$$
\lim\limits_{x\to c^+} f(x) = f(c).
$$

To demonstrate, let's consider the function $y=f(x)$ defined on the interval $[-2,\infty)$ as shown below.

![](images/0b/0b625f271c8889466c2a19ed8a333b05e70c2e852058cc1d4469f428d761c799.png)

The function is **right-continuous** at $x=-2$ because

$$
\lim_{x\to -2^+}f(x) = 4 = f(-2).
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "9424b0a9-43f3-5c35-b8b9-b78b9c69e816" :tutorial/math-academy-id 2597 :tutorial/title "Right Continuity"} {:db/id 17592186069577 :step/content {:db/id 17592186069962 :tutorial/content "Recall that a function $f(x)$ is said to be **continuous** at a point $x=c$ if 

$$
\lim\limits_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c) .
$$

In order for the above statement to be true, we require both

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {c}^{-}}f(x)=f(c)\,\text{and}\,{lim}_{x\to {c}^{+}}f(x)=f(c).\end{aligned}
$$

The above equalities represent left-continuity and right-continuity. So, we have the following fact:

> A function is **continuous** at a point if and only if it is *both* **left-continuous** *and* **right-continuous** at that point." :tutorial/id #uuid "1dd8ea3c-49f9-5c85-98b3-85b0542e7a8f" :tutorial/math-academy-id 2641 :tutorial/title "Defining Continuity in Terms of Left-Continuity and Right-Continuity"} :step/id #uuid "c70c04f3-5555-555a-93b3-8518806961e9" :step/math-academy-id 12456 :step/next {:db/id 17592186069575}} {:db/id 17592186069575 :step/content {:db/id 17592186068700 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186068552 :question/id #uuid "1ec6e675-6052-5cec-8b29-766084245f74" :question/math-academy-id "e-3591"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "81247553-750f-5bf7-a1c4-698ad63b5ae4" :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186069312} {:db/id 17592186069313} {:db/id 17592186234080} {:db/id 17592186234335} {:db/id 17592186234336} {:db/id 17592186240855} {:db/id 17592186240856} {:db/id 17592186326681} {:db/id 17592186326691} {:db/id 17592186341908} {:db/id 17592186341909}] :knowledge-point/title "Identifying True Statements Regarding Left- and Right-Continuity"} :step/id #uuid "1017d5f3-a1be-5979-aa84-1860d0b66f77" :step/math-academy-id 12121} {:db/id 17592186069962 :tutorial/content "Recall that a function $f(x)$ is said to be **continuous** at a point $x=c$ if
